Senses.Explanation: A command to go clean one's eating bowl after the meal; Zhaozhou Congshen gives it as his closing reply to a newcomer asking for instruction. The newcomer has said that he ate his gruel, and the record reports that he awakened after this reply. Zhaozhou's own record also uses the gruel question and exact command after a question about the student's own self. Later masters reopen the line. Dahui Zonggao says that many places raised and annotated it, restates washing the bowl without the final imperative, and asks whether instruction was given. Foyan Qingyuan says he ate gruel and washed his bowl that morning but did not awaken, then asks why. Wuwei Zongtai answers an entering interview with the exact command and is told that he knows the road's affair but not its flavor. Baohua Xian calls the exact command drawing legs on a snake. An ordinary cleanup command thereby becomes a stable, attributable public-case line repeatedly quoted, reenacted, and challenged.
